title: Aquí nadie dice tú
desc: A boy of twelve corrects your Spanish, kindly
setting: You are sitting on the step with Roberto and you have just used a word you learned from a book.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ideay, ¿por qué me habla así? Aquí nadie dice tú.
steps.en: Ideay, why are you talking to me like that? Nobody here says tú.

options.en: Oh, no? And how do you say it?
options.feedback: You let a child of twelve teach you. That is how nearly all of this gets learned, and he will remember that you asked.

options.en: Sorry, that is how I learned it.
options.feedback: Honest, but it closes the door. He was offering to fix it for you.

options.en: That is how you say it in Spanish.
options.feedback: You have just told a Nicaraguan how his own language works. It is also not true here.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Se dice vos. Vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos.
steps.en: You say vos. Vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos.

options.es: Vos tenés. Vos querés. Ya, así.
options.en: Vos tenés. Vos querés. Right, like that.
options.feedback: Say it back out loud. The accent is the whole difference between comés and comes, and your ear needs it more than your eye does.
Understood is not the same as said. Repeating it once now saves you a month.

options.en: It is the same thing, no?
options.feedback: It is not. Tú marks you as foreign in every sentence you say for as long as you keep it.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Pero a mi mamá no le diga vos. A ella usted.
steps.en: But do not say vos to my mother. To her, usted.

options.es: Entonces a ella usted y a vos vos.
options.en: So usted to her and vos to you.
options.feedback: That is the rule in one sentence: vos for the people beside you, usted for the people above you.
Correct as far as it goes. The half you left out is the half you will get wrong.
Good question, and the answer is usted. Ask it out loud like that and people will keep telling you.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Dale pues, a ver. Hablame con vos.
steps.en: Go on then, let us hear it. Talk to me with vos.

options.es: ¿Vos querés ir a la pulpería conmigo?
options.en: Do you want to come to the pulpería with me?
options.feedback: Querés, not quieres, and you used it on the person who just taught it to you. That is the fastest way it sticks.
Right form, and he will take it. He asked for a sentence, not a declaration.
The verb is fine and the tú at the end undoes it. That pronoun is the tell.
